dossier.public_summary: A 13.9-day dip that is flat-bottomed and fits the small M dwarf in duration shows a significant second dip near phase 0.387 and a ~1.8x odd/even depth difference with large transit-to-transit scatter. With only three weak transits and no reliable centroid, the secondary and inconsistent depths point to a blended stellar eclipse rather than a 6.45 Rearth planet, flagged as planet-like by size alone but strongly EB-like by the other checks.

reasons.why: Depth not consistent across the 3 transits (chi2 6.526, dof 2) with share_of_top_3=1.0, favouring noise/few-event blend over a repeatable planet
ML planet rank far below 0.1 shows planet-like checks do not outweigh the odd secondary, variable depth and no centroid, as expected for false positives
Secondary at phase 0.3873 depth_ppm 8937 (depth_over_dip 0.3695) well above best_brightening_snr 2.988, not a hot-giant occultation but a stellar eclipse
No sector with a clear difference image (centroid_all not_run) and neighbours.could_cause 120, could_cause_within_1px 2, cannot positionally rule out a blend on the target
